settings.page.interface.subtitle: Font, scaling, language and motion preferences. The ECL brand theme is fixed; there is no theme color or light mode.
settings.page.interface.font.bundledNote: This list only contains font families that are bundled with ECL and verified for internal family name and real faces. This version ships HarmonyOS Sans SC (Regular / Medium / Bold); more families appear here only after licensing and verification, and arbitrary font files cannot be imported.
settings.page.interface.scale.note: Range 80%–150% in 5% steps. The window and its minimum size change by the same ratio and are finally limited by the screen work area; pages only shrink inside their own scroll containers, and Windows display scaling, resolution and system fonts are not modified.
settings.page.interface.scale.failed: Could not save the interface scale: {0}
settings.page.interface.language.restart: A language change takes full effect after restarting ECL; text already loaded in this window is not updated immediately. The language does not affect Minecraft instances, resource packs or the system language.
settings.page.interface.motion.note: When off, page transitions, panel expansion and button feedback jump straight to their final state. Status messages, progress, focus and error feedback are unaffected, as are downloads, installations and launches.
settings.page.interface.motion.systemNot: Windows has the "reduce animation" preference enabled, so ECL keeps interface motion off until that system preference changes.
settings.page.interface.boundaries.title: Fixed boundaries of interface preferences
settings.page.interface.boundary.theme.r: The ECL brand purple is a fixed product identity color; there is no theme color picker, theme pack or light/dark mode switch.
settings.page.interface.boundary.fontSiz: Text size only changes as a whole tier; the hierarchy of headings, body text and secondary text stays with the design system, so per-control size, spacing, corner radius or shadow editing is not offered.
settings.page.interface.boundary.fontFil: Only bundled fonts that are licensed and face-verified are used; there is no font file import, system font installation or font download.
settings.page.interface.boundary.display: Interface scaling and text size only affect ECL itself and never modify Windows display scaling, resolution, system fonts or the system language.
settings.page.interface.boundary.gameLan: The interface language only affects ECL; it does not change the language, resource packs or save configuration of any Minecraft instance.
settings.page.interface.boundary.motionP: Motion durations and easing are fixed by the design system (ADR 0021); the page only offers the on/off preference and no per-item animation parameter editing.
settings.page.java.subtitle: Manage the Java runtimes ECL can use and adjust the order used for automatic selection. ECL skips Java that does not meet the current instance's requirements.
settings.page.game.subtitle: Global launch defaults used when an instance has no explicit override.
settings.page.game.memory.groupNote: Global default policy; memory set explicitly in the instance workspace takes precedence. Automatic allocation is computed by the launch service from currently available memory; a manual value is kept but inactive while the policy is automatic.
settings.page.game.memory.autoUnavailabl: System memory could not be read, so automatic allocation temporarily uses {0}; launching keeps this conservative value.
settings.page.game.memory.manualPressure: The manual value {0} exceeds the currently available memory {1} and may cause system memory pressure.
settings.page.game.memory.algorithmNote: Automatic allocation is derived from currently available physical memory and reserved system headroom; it does not use a fixed share of total physical memory and does not take the game version as an input (there is no verifiable version rule).
settings.page.game.memory.overrideNote: Memory explicitly set on an instance always takes precedence over this default; clearing the instance value returns to the global policy.
settings.page.game.jvm.note: Global JVM arguments only apply when an instance has no arguments of its own; arguments required by ECL launching are never removed. Static checks are limited and cannot guarantee that the JVM will start.
settings.page.game.window.note: Width and height are validated and saved as one group; the default window size is kept while fullscreen is enabled and used again when it is turned off. ECL does not change the Windows resolution, DPI or display scaling.
settings.page.game.window.failed: Could not save the game window settings: {0}
settings.page.game.window.applied: Game window settings applied; they take effect on the next launch.
settings.page.game.launch.note: This page only manages launch defaults; it offers no switch to skip required launch checks or ignore errors. ECL window behavior after launch belongs to General, and changes apply to future launches.
settings.page.game.boundaries.title: Fixed boundaries of launch behavior
settings.page.game.boundary.skipChecks.r: The launch flow must verify instance validity, Java, required files and dependencies; this page offers no global switch to skip all checks or force any launch.
settings.page.game.boundary.eclWindow.re: Showing, minimizing or closing ECL after the game starts is handled by the General page and the ADR 0039 lifecycle; it is not duplicated here.
settings.page.game.boundary.systemDispla: ECL does not change the Windows resolution, DPI or display scaling; the page only provides the game window launch defaults.
Memory, JVM arguments and window settings apply to future launches; they do not modify an already running game process.
settings.page.downloads.subtitle: Global download policy, concurrency, speed limit and failure retry; search, queues and installation still live in the download center.
Download and install stages are not separated in every flow, so no ineffective option is shown.
settings.page.downloads.gap.integrity.re: The download service always verifies size and hash; the page offers no option to disable, skip or mark unverified files as trusted.
settings.page.downloads.gap.mirror.title: Custom mirror addresses
settings.page.downloads.gap.mirror.reaso: The mirror root is managed by the four-tier download source strategy; the page exposes no editable mirror URL, mirror list or private source.
settings.page.downloads.gap.cache.title: Download cache location
settings.page.downloads.gap.cache.reason: The cache location is managed by the Storage and paths page and is not duplicated here.

settings.page.storage.row.data.title: ECL data directory
settings.page.storage.row.data.descripti: Root for configuration, accounts, logs and caches; determined by portable mode, ECL_DATA_DIR or the installation location.
settings.page.storage.row.cache.title: Download cache directory

settings.page.storage.row.downloads.desc: Downloaded modpacks and similar artifacts; follows the ECL data directory and cannot be configured separately in this version.
settings.page.storage.row.logs.title: Log and diagnostics directory
settings.page.storage.row.logs.descripti: Runtime logs and diagnostic packages; follows the ECL data directory and cannot be configured separately in this version.
settings.page.storage.row.runtimes.title: Java runtime directory

settings.page.storage.row.program.title: Program files directory
settings.page.storage.row.program.descri: The ECL program itself; managed by the installer and operating system, with no editing entry.

settings.page.storage.boundaries.title: Fixed boundaries of storage and paths
settings.page.storage.boundary.dataDir.r: The data directory is determined by portable mode, ECL_DATA_DIR or the installation location. This version has no domain workflow for migrating configuration, accounts or logs, so it is shown read-only.
settings.page.storage.boundary.cache.tit: Configuring the download cache or temporary directory separately
settings.page.storage.boundary.cache.rea: Caches and download artifacts always follow the ECL data directory; two separate editable settings would not match the real paths.
settings.page.storage.boundary.program.t: Changing the location of program files or protected components
settings.page.storage.boundary.program.r: Program files, the installer and protected components are managed by the installer/operating system; ECL offers no editing entry.
settings.page.storage.boundary.cleanup.t: Deleting caches or cleaning instances on this page

settings.page.additions.authorization.no: Installation and updates show a plan and require a second confirmation. The per-capability authorization dialog from ADR 0053 (including the five-second reading buffer) is not implemented: addition manifests declare no capabilities, and the host keeps no grant records or call-boundary checks. This page therefore shows no permission list, offers no trust-all switch, and claims no sandbox isolation.
settings.page.additions.boundaries.title: Fixed boundaries of addition permissions and isolation
settings.page.additions.boundary.permiss: ADR 0053 is approved but its implementation has not started: manifests contain no capability declarations or purposes, the host keeps no grant records, and there are no call-boundary checks. This page therefore shows no permission list, offers no per-capability consent, and offers no trust-all/unlimited-permission switch.
settings.page.additions.boundary.sandbox: Additions load in the same process as ECL through an AssemblyLoadContext, with no operating-system isolation or resource limits. Until isolation is verified, this page does not claim that additions are sandboxed.
settings.page.additions.boundary.registr: Official addition registry and manifest governance

ADR 0054 is not implemented: there is no docs/additions registry or manifest governance, so this page never constructs an online catalog; only an explicitly configured, signature-verified catalog is read.
settings.page.additions.boundary.publish: Only catalog signatures and per-file SHA-256 checks inside a package exist; there is no separate publisher identity verification or update channel. This page shows no trusted-publisher badge, and user consent can never bypass a signature or integrity failure.
